description: We are a group of enthusiastic students participating in a NASA Challenge. We are passionate about science, technology, space exploration, and innovation. We enjoy sharing ideas, solving problems, and learning new things. We are looking for creative, motivated, and responsible team members with skills in coding, engineering, research, design, and problem-solving. Most importantly, we value teamwork, communication, and a willingness to learn. Join us and let's create something amazing together!
summary:
Ro’ya: Al-Bader Expedition is an interactive lunar exploration and astronaut training game designed primarily for children aged 7–12, while also welcoming students, educators, and space enthusiasts.

Players become astronauts, create their own characters, establish a lunar outpost, manage essential life-support resources, and respond to mission challenges such as solar storms. Through simulations and decision-making, they learn how to maintain a safe and successful expedition. The experience also features a Space Academy, interactive exploration of the Moon, Earth, and stars, and ASTRA, an AI-powered assistant that provides guidance, explanations, and age-appropriate hints.

Our project addresses NASA's Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge by transforming space education into an immersive, hands-on experience. Rather than simply learning about astronauts, players experience their responsibilities through mission simulations, resource management, scientific exploration, and problem-solving. We also integrate authentic scientific resources, including NASA solar-flare records, lunar imagery, and astronomical star-catalogue data, connecting gameplay with real-world space science.

Ro’ya makes space exploration more accessible, engaging, and educational. It encourages critical thinking, scientific curiosity, and learning through experimentation, inspiring the next generation of scientists, engineers, and space explorers.
details:
1. What exactly does it do?

Ro’ya: Al-Bader Expedition is an interactive lunar exploration and astronaut training game designed primarily for children aged 7–12, while also welcoming students, educators, and anyone interested in space, astronomy, and exploration.

Players create their own astronaut and embark on three main missions: establishing a lunar outpost, managing life-support resources, and surviving a solar storm. They make decisions involving oxygen, water, food, power, equipment, and astronaut safety. The experience also includes a Space Academy with additional hands-on challenges, an exploration map featuring the Moon, Earth, and stars, and ASTRA, our AI-powered mission assistant, which provides child-friendly explanations and hints without completing activities for players.

2. How does it work?

Each mission combines a briefing, interactive activities, scientific questions, and feedback. Players make decisions, complete challenges, and learn from the consequences of their choices. Progress is saved in the browser, allowing players to continue their expedition later. Stars, badges, and graduation insignias recognise achievements and encourage further learning.

The game also incorporates authentic scientific resources. NASA DONKI provides solar-flare records, NASA lunar imagery and elevation textures support the Moon's visual environment, and HYG/Hipparcos star-catalogue data supports the Celestial Observatory. Real scientific observations are clearly distinguished from simulated mission conditions and artistic visualisations.

3. What benefits does it have?

The project transforms space science into an engaging, hands-on learning experience. It develops critical thinking, problem-solving, resource management, scientific reasoning, and curiosity. Players can experiment, retry challenges, receive explanations, and learn from mistakes in a safe virtual environment.

To support different learning preferences, the experience includes narration, visual guidance, adjustable audio, and touch-friendly interactions, making space education more engaging and accessible.

4. What do you hope to achieve?

We aim to inspire children to see themselves as future astronauts, scientists, and engineers. Our goal is to make complex concepts such as lunar environments, life-support systems, and space weather understandable and exciting. Ultimately, we hope to nurture scientific curiosity and encourage the next generation to explore beyond Earth.

5. What tools and technologies did you use?

  • Lovable: AI-assisted development and live project previews.
  • TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS: Application logic, structure, and styling.
  • React and TanStack Start: Interactive web application and server-side functions.
  • Tailwind CSS: Interface styling and visual consistency.
  • Three.js and React Three Fiber: Interactive 3D lunar environments and the Celestial Observatory.
  • Matter.js and dnd-kit: Physics-based activities and drag-and-drop interactions.
  • Lovable AI Gateway: AI-powered responses for ASTRA.
  • NASA DONKI and NASA imagery: Solar-flare records and lunar visual resources.
  • HYG/Hipparcos and Natural Earth: Star-catalogue data and Earth geographical boundaries.
  • Browser Speech Synthesis and Web Audio: Narration, music, and sound effects.
  • Vitest and Playwright: Automated testing of game mechanics and player interactions.

The project runs directly in a web browser without requiring specialised hardware, making it accessible across supported devices.
